_comment: Effective QSOFITMORE configuration for the SDSS/eFEDS QSO 04592649654_z_0.5874. The executable runner is Tools/qsofitmore_line/main.py; this file is the reviewable switch record. Every fit switch below is passed explicitly to qsofitmore.QSOFitNew.Fit.

coverage.coverage_note: The SDSS COADD spans 3567-10335 A observed, i.e. 2247-6510 A at z=0.587413. H-alpha (6564.61 A rest) and the UV C III]/C IV complexes fall outside this range. They remain in the table for UV/higher-z spectra and are skipped by qsofitmore's complex selection.

fit.dust_law: Fitzpatrick (1999) f99law, R_V=3.1, as implemented in qsofitmore.extinction
fit.wave_range_note: Rest-frame clean coverage of the SDSS COADD after dropping zero-IVAR pixels. The upper edge is set just below H-alpha/NII6549 so a prepared PyQSOFit copy (which sanitises zero-IVAR pixels) cannot pull the H-alpha complex into the fit.

line_table.source: qsofitmore/examples/output/qsopar_log.csv at the pinned commit, with the [O III] 4959/5007 and outflow doublet flux ratios tied (findex=1/2, fvalue=0.33/1.00) and narrow C III]/C IV rows added for UV coverage. H-alpha/C III]/C IV rows are retained for general use and are automatically skipped when their rest wavelength is outside the observed rest-frame coverage.

switches.BC: Balmer continuum (Dietrich et al. 2002) plus the Storey & Hummer (1995) high-order Balmer series (n_upper=6-50) at log10(n_e)=9. This is the package's Balmer-continuum/high-order-Balmer capability.
switches.Fe_verner09: Kept True together with iron_temp_name=V09 so qsofitmore.Fe_line_prop uses the V09 template when integrating the requested Fe II bands. This is the package's compatibility switch; qsofitmore warns that it is ignored when iron_temp_name is set, but the flag is still stored and is required for the Fe II band-flux columns.
switches.broken_pl: Two-slope power law. The 4661 A break lies inside 2247-6510 A, so qsofitmore selects its optical profile (3000 A pivot, 4661 A break). The blue and red slopes are both free.
switches.decomposition_host: Disabled. qsofitmore's Yip+2004 host decomposition restricts the rest-frame grid to about >=3450 A and would remove Mg II; the host is measured independently by pPXF in the repo.
switches.deredden: SFD98 E(B-V) at the source coordinates, Fitzpatrick (1999) R_V=3.1 extinction; line fluxes are dereddened. The measured E(B-V) is recorded in qsofitmore_continuum.csv.
switches.include_iron: Enables the Fe II pseudo-continuum. With iron_temp_name=V09 the Verner et al. (2009) template (2000-10000 A) is used.
switches.n_trails: Number of independent noise realizations per fitted complex (and for the continuum MC). 200 is 200x the package default of 1 and twice the PyQSOFit MC in this repo.
switches.poly: Disabled because the broken power law already provides the large-scale curvature and an extra polynomial is not identifiable over this short lever arm.
switches.rej_abs: Disabled; the SDSS mask and calibrated errors already remove bad pixels. Enabling it did not change the H-beta/Mg II totals in the pre-run checks.
switches.tie_flux_1: Ties the [O III] 4959 core amplitude to 0.33 of 5007 (group 1).
switches.tie_flux_2: Ties the [O III] 4959 outflow amplitude to 0.33 of 5007 (group 2).
switches.tie_lambda: Ties line centres within a kinematics group to the first member of the group.
switches.tie_width: Ties Gaussian widths within a kinematics group. H-beta narrow and [O III] share group 1; the [O III] outflow wings share group 2.

systematics.note: After the primary V09 run the runner also performs a least-squares (MC off) BG92-VW01 fit to quantify the Fe II template systematic. The alternate result is written to systematics/ and is not used for the headline measurements.

uncertainty.mcmc_note: qsofitmore 1.2.2 does not implement an emcee/MCMC sampler. Its native uncertainty mode is the lmfit Monte Carlo refit used here; no MCMC is claimed.
uncertainty.mode: parametric Monte Carlo: add N(0, err) to every fitted pixel and refit the continuum and each line complex with lmfit
uncertainty.package_broad_narrow_note: qsofitmore classifies every fitted Gaussian by sigma > 1200 km/s for its <comp>_whole_br_area columns. Multi-Gaussian broad templates can contain individual Gaussians below that cut. The compact table therefore recomputes each physical line total from all of its Gaussian components; the package columns are retained in qsofitmore_result.csv and qsofitmore_components.csv for inspection.

upstream.citation: Fu et al., qsofitmore (PyQSOFit derivative); see upstream CITATION and README
